ff1c026be45ed0454ad8.text: This module is written to suit your language needs as a Grade 8 learner. It is here to

0e27c59268a7a5181ac5.text: help you master skills that will allow you to appropriately and responsibly communicate your thoughts and feelings especially in this time when different information and issues arise. Hence, there is a need for you to learn how to properly respond and express your opinions on issues that you may experience in society.

996d77a74afe25690928.text: Have you ever encountered any issues that you want to give your opinion? Were you

419781929f8810f867e5.text: able to communicate your feelings clearly? How?

ec59d0c4d8de61e15824.text: Perhaps, you have tried doing it in different ways; however, there might also be

32354ed145af7767b66e.text: moments that made you feel that it is difficult to express your ideas especially in English. Thus, this module will help you learn different ways to communicate your emotions and reactions to certain issues.

ed13eda2e83d02e14598.text: The Most Essential Learning Competency (MELC) covered in this module is use a

bcd3ff0f4be0a6010f29.text: range of verbs, adjectives, and adverbs to convey emotional response or reactions to an issue to persuade.

7e2a4b0b682f10eee688.text: As a learner of this module, you are expected to:

5137ef2bf44e28bc0a8a.text: • identify the appropriate verbs, adjectives, and adverbs used in conveying emotions and opinions for persuasion; • use appropriate verbs, adjectives, and adverbs in expressing emotions and opinions for persuasion; and • write a persuasive paragraph using verbs, adjectives, and adverbs.

bbbc4abb8b92a676e1bd.text: Sample sentences taken from the dialogue:

bf43c11f4275fe4e5f3b.text: 1. You better stay home. The possibility of you getting sick scares me.

4e2f2b2f6b5c9fa48e39.text: (The verb “scarefs” is used to state the unpleasant emotion towards the possibility of getting sick. Stating an emotion is a way in convincing someone.)

e19147e5a706fa7fadbf.text: 2. No, Noel. I strongly disagree. You should follow what I tell you. (The verb disagree states the stand of the speaker. Emphasizing a stand is a good way in influencing someone to agree with your ideas.)

0155eb8538486992002a.text: In Module 3, you have learned that modal verbs have different uses. The modals

54da19d03422f6584727.text: given below are verbs that express suggestion or recommendation which is an effective way to convince or persuade. To further clarify the difference of each modal, they are arranged from weakest to strongest in terms of expressing a suggestion or recommendation. Furthermore, the table shows their functions and examples.

6ab92399e938bb1f4c42.text: Type of  Functions Examples  Verb     Modals    Could   It is used to give a suggestion which a person may or may not follow. I suggest you play with your brother and sister or you could join me pray for your Tatay’s safety. (The modal could is used to give a suggestion that the person could join the speaker in praying.) Should   It is also used to give a suggestion but more insistent than the modal could. No, Noel. I strongly disagree. You should follow what I tell you. (The modal should is used to suggest that the person needs to follow what the speaker tells.)
rows: It is used to give a suggestion which a person may or may not follow.
I suggest you play with your brother and sister or you could join me pray for your Tatay’s safety. (The modal could is used to give a suggestion that the person could join the speaker in praying.)
It is also used to give a suggestion but more insistent than the modal could.
No, Noel. I strongly disagree. You should follow what I tell you. (The modal should is used to suggest that the person needs to follow what the speaker tells.)
It is used to formally give an advice or a recommendation usually coming from an expert.
The Department of Health (DOH) recommends that people ought to stay at home so that they will not get sick. (The modal ought to is used to formally suggest that staying at home is important.)
It is used to give a recommendation by presenting the possible negative consequence if the advice is not followed.

During the Enhanced Community Quarantine (ECQ), you had better wear your mask in public places or the police will arrest you. (The modal had better is used since the possible negative consequence, the police will arrest you, is presented to serve as a warning.)
It is used to show a strong obligation that needs to be followed.

The government must control the people’s movement in public to stop the spread of the virus. (The modal must is used to express the strong obligation of the government in taking action against the spread of the virus.)
a34f9d0bf19ef55a5524.text: Ought to It is used to formally give an advice or a recommendation usually coming from an expert. The Department of Health (DOH) recommends that people ought to stay at home so that they will not get sick. (The modal ought to is used to formally suggest that staying at home is important.) Had better It is used to give a recommendation by presenting the possible negative consequence if the advice is not followed. During the Enhanced Community Quarantine (ECQ), you had better wear your mask in public places or the police will arrest you. (The modal had better is used since the possible negative consequence, the police will arrest you, is presented to serve as a warning.) Must It is used to show a strong obligation that needs to be followed. The government must control the people’s movement in public to stop the spread of the virus. (The modal must is used to express the strong obligation of the government in taking action against the spread of the virus.)

6a10360ebe02b8623d91.text: emotions and reactions. This time, you will learn a set of adjectives that can also help tell your emotions on a certain issue.

e599097a4911561b5569.text: In Lesson 1 and Lesson 2, you were introduced to using a range of verbs and

b961216cbcc07cca172d.text: adjectives in expressing your emotions and opinions. This time you will learn about adverbs.

ee84ec59248067415d36.text: The sentences below are based on the Story of the Aged Mother. Try to compare

0037f21838ec95b4a1bd.text: them and take note of their differences.

labels.text: I agree that old people must
The farmer in the story was

652244215b8acbe4fe76.text: I agree that old people must  be respected and protected.  The farmer in the story was  happy that her mother saved  the people.

labels.text: The farmer in the story was

cddcc83c30d46e38c3c6.text: strongly  agree that old  people must be respected and  protected.  The farmer in the story was  really  happy that her mother  saved the people.

294a142ab35f45e755ae.text: What is the difference between sentence 1 and sentence 2? How about sentence 3

aae08bfb6c19df9a7600.text: and sentence 4? Which sentences sound more convincing to you?

d9a159505188a772b034.text: Notice that sentences 2 contains the words “strongly”. This word gives a higher

7b6a416f1181b65a1b2a.text: emotional degree on the verb agree. Also, take note that sentence 4 contains the word “really”. This word emphasizes that the happiness felt by the farmer is more intense than the happiness expressed in sentence 1.

3b06b6fcef30a2230515.text: The words “strongly” and “really” are examples of adverbs. They describe verbs,

d69aab364761b3d02937.text: adjectives, and another adverb. There are many types of adverbs but in this lesson, you will focus on adverbs that can give emphasis on your responses and reactions. They are called adverbs of opinion.

506ca0ef39a4d545ad2f.text: This type of adverbs emphasizes the intensity of your stand or opinion. They help

9109f0081803c4019d9b.text: clarify your belief about a certain issue.

998aadd8d078dcf18908.text: The following are the commonly used adverbs of opinion:

61cd05dfe78c5ca9ba37.text: Take note on how some of the adverbs above are used in the following sentences:

0f894ec707fdc0215584.text: 1. Clearly, the farmer in the story loved her old mother. He showed this by

ea873ce9b2ceab404d18.text: protecting and hiding his mother from the cruel governor.

acb90cca1ed48527e5ba.text: (The adverb clearly emphasizes that the farmer’s love to his old mother is very clear in the story. The adverb clearly is placed at the beginning of the sentence. This means that they can be placed at the beginning of sentences and are followed with a comma.)

ea0b492ff18d704a354e.text: 2. Minors and senior citizens must stay at home during the pandemic. We

86b99091c775ad4d70e0.text: definitely need to follow this health measure to protect them.

53fc1c29d93742c24e29.text: (The adverb definitely emphasizes the stand of the speaker that he or she is certain that the health measure must be followed. The adverb definitely is placed before the verb need. This means that they can also be placed before the main verb.)

45f1d7c3e9012f14d39e.text: 3. Filipinos’ sense of respect to old people is evidently shown on how they protect and care for their old family members. (The adverb evidently emphasizes the observation of the speaker that Filipinos’ sense of respect to old people is clearly seen on how they treat old family members. The adverb is placed in between the word are and doing. This means that they can be placed between an auxiliary verb and a main verb.)

6abbb2ab67ff7d3e32be.text: Furthermore, adverbs of opinion can also be in a form of phrases. The table below

fb3e91ea7ca76c7d5a86.text: shows some of the commonly used phrases that function as an adverb of opinion. From my view

d200df92776b81be8244.text: Take a look at how they are used in a sentence.

8abcd342f41f7ec1bfc1.text: Filipinos are really respectful and polite to old people. Without a doubt, filial piety

7db7870b980c1165fb1d.text: has been always part of our culture.

296a2b72ec6ee5177228.text: (The phrase without a doubt shows the firm feelings of the speaker that filial piety or respect to elders has always been a part of our culture. The phrase is placed at the beginning of the sentence. This means that they are usually placed at the beginning of a sentence and followed by a comma.)

6e02f7052e942e7aafc3.text: Adverbs of opinion can also help emphasize the ideas in your paragraph especially if

d586390f96bc89ff39f6.text: you want to convince readers about your opinion to an issue.
